plan: With 3 bidders total (including myself) and the ascending clock mechanism where the sealed bid acts as an automatic exit point, this functions like a second-price auction. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, so bidding my true value of $24 ensures I only win when profitable and never overpay relative to my value.

Since the sealed bid acts as my automatic exit price in an ascending clock auction, this mimics a second-price auction structure: I win only if my bid is highest, and I pay the second-highest bid. The dominant strategy in such mechanisms is to bid my true value, as this ensures I win whenever the price is below my value (profitable) and avoid winning when it's above my value (unprofitable). Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus, bidding exactly $9 is optimal.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the clock mechanism means I pay the second-highest bid if I win), my dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down given the mechanics described.
